:::{#sol-flat-point-compare}

The prediction $3.98$ (@sol-flat-point-predict)
and the exact [value](functions.qmd#def-value) $3.9801$ (@sol-flat-point-exact)
differ by $0.0001$,
which is $\smallconst^2$.
For this $f$, the error of the [linear approximation](calculus.qmd#def-linear-approximation) at any $w$ is exactly

$$
f(w + \smallconst) - [f(w) + f'(w)\,\smallconst] = \smallconst^2,
$$

so halving the step quarters the error.

A step of [gradient descent](optimization.qmd#def-gradient-descent) with step length $s$
changes $w$ by $\smallconst = -s f'(w)$.
The linear approximation predicts the change $-s\,f'(w)^2$ in $f$,
and the error is $\smallconst^2 = s^2 f'(w)^2$,
so the actual change is $-s\,f'(w)^2\,(1 - s)$.
This change is negative, that is, $f$ decreases, exactly when $0 < s < 1$, for $f'(w) \ne 0$:
the error is smaller than the predicted decrease only for a short enough step.

:::
